the multicast-DNS decision, stated globally and again for the interface it already applies to. resolved's compiled-in MulticastDNS default is yes and Debian's drop-in turning it off is one this composition drops, so an interface that 80-dhcp.network's Name=eth* does not match fell back to the global and advertised on the customer's LAN -- measured on a booted guest as Global yes, eth0 no, sit0 YES. The global makes the unnamed case fail safe; the per-interface drop-in declares what eth* already resolves to, so nothing that works today changes

systemd's postinst creates this link directly, so no package owns it and deb-systemd-helper has no record of it -- both of the composer's proofs miss it and it falls out, while 90-systemd.preset says `enable systemd-pstore.service`. Dropping it ships the collector without the harvester: the kernel writes crash records into /sys/fs/pstore and nothing moves them out. THE HARVEST IS THE BOUND, not a diagnostic extra -- a pstore backend does not roll over, so one unharvested crash can stop the next being recorded, and on efi-pstore the records sit in firmware variables until the kernel starts refusing writes
